name: DialUpSoundz
tagline: Talk a playlist through with Claude, then save it to Apple Music.
summary: Paste the list Claude gives you. DialUpSoundz finds every song on Apple Music, shows you what it matched, and saves the playlist to your library or plays it right away. It's also the start of a personal layer over Apple Music, with your listening history, your own ratings and an early dashboard, all kept on your iPhone.
statusLabel: Coming soon to the App Store
stepsHeading: From a chat to a playlist

steps.title: Talk it through with Claude
steps.body: Copy the DialUpSoundz prompt into a chat with Claude. Talk about moods, eras, deep cuts and what to leave out, then ask for the list.

steps.title: Paste the list
steps.body: Copy Claude's reply and paste it into DialUpSoundz. A plain list such as Artist - Song, one per line, works too.

steps.title: Review the matches
steps.body: Each song, artist or album is looked up on Apple Music. Anything that needs a look is marked, and you can swap versions, preview, reorder or remove.

steps.title: Save
steps.body: Nothing is saved until you tap Save. The playlist goes to your Apple Music library with its name and description.

features.title: Playlists from Claude's list
features.body: Original studio versions are preferred over live, karaoke and cover versions, unless you asked for those.

features.title: Album lists
features.body: Ask Claude for whole albums instead of songs, and DialUpSoundz matches each one to the album on Apple Music.

features.title: Play in full
features.body: Play a draft or a saved playlist right in the app, with a now-playing bar and AirPlay.

features.title: Listen Later
features.body: Keep songs and albums you want to come back to. Open one to see its songs, mark it listened, and say how it was.

features.title: Your own ratings
features.body: Rate albums and songs from 1 to 5 stars, love them or mark them not for me, and add tags and notes. Hand Claude a summary so its picks lean your way.

features.title: Listening history and dashboard
features.body: The app records what you play from the day you install it, and can import years of Apple's play history. The dashboard is early and growing.
